question:
A series is given with one term wrong. Select the wrong term from the given alternatives.

-203, -206, -209, -212, -215, -218, -221, -226
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. -226.

GIVEN

• -203, -206, -209, -212, -215, -218, -221, -226

SOLUTION

• Each term decreases by 3: -203, -206, -209, -212, -215, -218, -221, -224.

• The last given term is -226, but it should be -224. So -226 is wrong.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Constant difference of -3 throughout; the term that breaks the -3 step is the odd one (-221 - 3 = -224, not -226).

NOTE

• In wrong-term series, first find the common difference/ratio from the majority of terms, then spot the single term that violates it.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

Z, T, ?, G, Z, T, M, G, Z
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. M.

GIVEN

• Z, T, ?, G, Z, T, M, G, Z

SOLUTION

• The block Z, T, M, G repeats: (Z, T, ?, G)(Z, T, M, G)(Z...).

• Comparing the first block with the second, the missing term matches M.

• So ? = M.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Recognise the repeating 4-letter cycle Z-T-M-G; the blank sits at the 3rd slot = M.

NOTE

• For repeating-pattern series, split the string into equal blocks and align positions to read off the missing letter.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fifth letter cluster in the same way as the second letter cluster is related to the first letter cluster and fourth letter cluster is related to third letter cluster.

VD : EW :: GM : TN :: KB : ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. PY.

GIVEN

• VD : EW :: GM : TN :: KB : ?

SOLUTION

• Each letter is replaced by its opposite (complement: sum of positions = 27).

• VD → V(22)→E(5), D(4)→W(23) = EW. GM → G(7)→T(20), M(13)→N(14) = TN.

• KB → K(11)→P(16), B(2)→Y(25) = PY.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Opposite-letter pairs (A↔Z, B↔Y, ...); position + partner = 27. Apply to K→P and B→Y.

NOTE

• Learn the complement pairs: EJOTY and their mirrors help spot 'opposite letter' coding instantly.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

EY, HB, MF, PI, UM, XP, ?, FW
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. CT.

GIVEN

• EY, HB, MF, PI, UM, XP, ?, FW

SOLUTION

• First letters: E(+3)H(+5)M(+3)P(+5)U(+3)X(+5)?(+3)F — X+5 = C, then C+3 = F. So first = C.

• Second letters: Y(+3)B(+4)F(+3)I(+4)M(+3)P(+4)?(+3)W — P+4 = T, then T+3 = W. So second = T.

• ? = CT.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Two alternating gaps: first-letter +3/+5, second-letter +3/+4. Next step gives C and T.

NOTE

• Split each two-letter cluster into separate columns and find each column's own pattern (letters wrap past Z).

question:
Select the option that is related to the third letter cluster in the same way as the second letter cluster is related to the first letter cluster and sixth letter cluster is related to fifth letter cluster.

EP : BK :: RK : ? :: UC : RX
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. OF.

GIVEN

• EP : BK :: RK : ? :: UC : RX

SOLUTION

• Pattern: first letter -3, second letter -5.

• EP → E(5)-3=B(2), P(16)-5=K(11) = BK. UC → U(21)-3=R(18), C(3)-5=X(24, wrap) = RX.

• RK → R(18)-3=O(15), K(11)-5=F(6) = OF.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Shift the two letters back by 3 and 5 respectively; R→O and K→F.

NOTE

• When decoding backwards past A, wrap around (A→Z...) using mod 26.

question:
In the following question, set of letter clusters are given. The letter clusters of each set are related to the letter clusters of the same set by some Logic/Rule/Relation. From the given alternatives, select a group of letter clusters which follows the same Logic/Rule/Relation.

(LU, OX, RA)

(WX, ZA, CD)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. (BH, EK, HN).

GIVEN

• (LU, OX, RA) and (WX, ZA, CD)

SOLUTION

• Rule: from cluster to cluster, the first letter increases by +3 and the second letter increases by +3.

• LU→OX→RA: L,O,R (+3) and U,X,A (+3). WX→ZA→CD: W,Z,C (+3) and X,A,D (+3).

• Check options: (BH, EK, HN): B,E,H (+3) and H,K,N (+3). Both hold → (BH, EK, HN).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Only need +3 on both letters across the three clusters; test each option's first and second letters for a constant +3.

NOTE

• Ignore the internal gap within a pair; the classification rule here is the step between successive clusters.

question: If 27 May 2024 is a Sunday, then what day will 28 November 2024 be?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. Wednesday.

GIVEN

• 27 May 2024 = Sunday; find the day on 28 November 2024.

SOLUTION

• Days from 27 May to 28 Nov: May 4 + Jun 30 + Jul 31 + Aug 31 + Sep 30 + Oct 31 + Nov 28 = 185 days.

• 185 ÷ 7 = 26 remainder 3 odd days.

• Sunday + 3 = Wednesday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Add the day-gaps to the reference date, take the total mod 7, and count that many days forward from Sunday.

NOTE

• Odd days = remaining days after removing complete weeks; only the remainder shifts the weekday.

question: The calendar for the year 1986 will be the same as which of the following years?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 1997.

GIVEN

• Year whose calendar matches 1986.

SOLUTION

• Add odd days year by year from 1986 until the running total is a multiple of 7, and the target year is (like 1986) a non-leap year.

• 1986:1, 87:1, 88:2, 89:1, 90:1, 91:1, 92:2, 93:1, 94:1, 95:1, 96:2 → cumulative through 1996 = 14 ≡ 0.

• So 1997 repeats the 1986 calendar, and 1997 is also a non-leap year.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• A non-leap calendar usually repeats after 11 years (1986 + 11 = 1997) when the odd-day sum clears to 0.

NOTE

• Leap year = 2 odd days, ordinary year = 1; the repeat must also match leap/non-leap type.

question: A person was born on 3 October 2019. What day of the week will be on his 6th birthday?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. Friday.

GIVEN

• Born 3 October 2019; find the day on the 6th birthday (3 October 2025).

SOLUTION

• 3 October 2019 was a Thursday.

• From 2019 to 2025, leap Februaries counted are 2020 and 2024 → 2 extra days.

• 6 years = 6×365 + 2 = 2192 days; 2192 mod 7 = 1 odd day.

• Thursday + 1 = Friday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Odd days over N years = N + (number of leap days). Here 6 + 2 = 8 ≡ 1, so shift one day forward.

NOTE

• Count a Feb 29 only if it falls strictly between the two dates.

question: 5 boys P, Q, R, S and T are sitting in a row facing north (not necessarily in the same order). Q and R are immediate neighbours. S and R are immediate neighbours. Only P is to the left of Q. Who is sitting in the middle of the row?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. R.

GIVEN

• Row of 5 facing north; Q-R adjacent; S-R adjacent; only P is left of Q.

SOLUTION

• 'Only P to the left of Q' → P at position 1, Q at position 2.

• Q and R adjacent → R at position 3. S and R adjacent → S at position 4. T takes position 5.

• Order (left→right): P, Q, R, S, T. Middle (position 3) = R.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Fix P-Q at the left end, then chain R next to Q and S next to R; the middle seat lands on R.

NOTE

• 'Only X is to the left' means exactly one person sits left, pinning the second person to seat 2.

question: 7 males A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting in a row facing north (not necessarily in the same order). Only four males are to the left of A. B is the immediate neighbour of A and C. D is third to the left of E. F is not the immediate neighbour of E. What is the position of F from the right end of the row?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. Sixth.

GIVEN

• 7 males; only four to left of A; B between A and C; D third to left of E; F not adjacent to E.

SOLUTION

• Four males left of A → A at seat 5.

• B adjacent to A and C → A(5), B(6), C(7).

• D third to left of E in remaining seats {1,2,3,4}: D(1), E(4). F not adjacent to E(4), so F ≠ 3 → F(2), G(3).

• Arrangement: D, F, G, E, A, B, C. F is at seat 2 → from right end = 7-2+1 = 6th.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Place A at 5 (four to its left), block A-B-C at the right, then fit D...E gap of 3 in the left seats.

NOTE

• Position from right = (total + 1) - position from left.

question: 7 males A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting in a row facing north (not necessarily in the same order). Only four males are to the left of A. B is the immediate neighbour of A and C. D is third to the left of E. F is not the immediate neighbour of E. What is the position of D from the left end of the row?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. First.

GIVEN

• Same arrangement as Q31: four males left of A; B between A and C; D third to left of E; F not adjacent to E.

SOLUTION

• A at seat 5; A(5), B(6), C(7). Remaining {1,2,3,4}: D(1), E(4) [D third to left of E].

• F ≠ 3 (not adjacent to E) → F(2), G(3).

• Final: D, F, G, E, A, B, C. D is at seat 1 → First from the left.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• The 'D...E gap of 3' forces D to the extreme left seat once A-B-C occupy the right block.

NOTE

• 'Third to the left of E' means E is at D+3; count seats, not people between.

question:
Select the option that is related to the second letter-number cluster in the same way as the third letter-number cluster is related to the fourth letter-number cluster and fifth letter-number cluster is related to sixth letter-number cluster.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

? : AD200 :: WK500 : UG300 :: TO700 : RK500
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. CH400.

GIVEN

• ? : AD200 :: WK500 : UG300 :: TO700 : RK500

SOLUTION

• Relation (left→right): first letter -2, second letter -4, number -200.

• WK500→UG300: W-2=U, K-4=G, 500-200=300. TO700→RK500: T-2=R, O-4=K, 700-200=500.

• So ?-2 = A, ?-4 = D, ?-200 = 200 → first = C(3), second = H(8), number = 400 → CH400.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Reverse the known map: add back +2, +4 and +200 to AD200 to get the missing source = CH400.

NOTE

• Treat the number as a whole (no digit splitting) as the note instructs.

question:
Select the option that is related to the sixth letter-number cluster in the same way as the first letter-number cluster is related to the second letter-number cluster and third letter-number cluster is related to fourth letter-number cluster.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

ADK10 : ZCJ110 :: BLP60 : AKO160 :: ? : RIL190
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. SJM90.

GIVEN

• ADK10 : ZCJ110 :: BLP60 : AKO160 :: ? : RIL190

SOLUTION

• Relation: each letter -1, number +100.

• ADK10→ZCJ110: A-1=Z, D-1=C, K-1=J, 10+100=110. BLP60→AKO160: B-1=A, L-1=K, P-1=O, 60+100=160.

• So ? → RIL190 means ?-1 letters = R,I,L and ?+100 = 190. Reverse: R+1=S, I+1=J, L+1=M, 190-100=90 → SJM90.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Since the map is 'minus one letter, plus 100', undo it: add one letter and subtract 100 from RIL190 → SJM90.

NOTE

• Keep the number whole; only the letters shift by a fixed step.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and fourth number is related to third number.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

5165 : 5113 :: 8326 : 8274 :: 1671 : ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 1619.

GIVEN

• 5165 : 5113 :: 8326 : 8274 :: 1671 : ?

SOLUTION

• 5165 - 5113 = 52. 8326 - 8274 = 52.

• So the rule is subtract 52: 1671 - 52 = 1619.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Same constant gap (52) in every pair; subtract 52 from 1671.

NOTE

• Operate on the whole number, not its digits, as the note requires.

question:
Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and sixth number is related to fifth number.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

948 : 472 :: 702 : ? :: 600 : 298
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 349.

GIVEN

• 948 : 472 :: 702 : ? :: 600 : 298

SOLUTION

• Rule: (number ÷ 2) - 2.

• 948÷2 - 2 = 474 - 2 = 472. 600÷2 - 2 = 300 - 2 = 298.

• 702÷2 - 2 = 351 - 2 = 349.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Halve the number and drop 2; 702→351→349.

NOTE

• Verify a candidate rule on both given pairs before applying it to the missing one.

question: In a certain code language, 'SEVEN' is coded as '19522514' and 'EIGHT' is coded as '597820'. How will 'GAME' be coded in that code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 71135.

GIVEN

• SEVEN = 19522514, EIGHT = 597820.

SOLUTION

• Each letter is written as its alphabet position and the numbers are concatenated.

• SEVEN → 19,5,22,5,14 = 19522514. EIGHT → 5,9,7,8,20 = 597820.

• GAME → G=7, A=1, M=13, E=5 → 7,1,13,5 = 71135.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Replace letters by positions (A=1...Z=26) and string them together with no separators.

NOTE

• Two-digit positions (like 13, 20, 22) stay whole, which is why lengths vary.

question: In a certain coded language 'CAPUT' is coded as 'DCSQO' and 'ADOBO' is coded as 'BFRXJ'. How will 'DESKS' be coded in the same code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. EGVGN.

GIVEN

• CAPUT = DCSQO, ADOBO = BFRXJ.

SOLUTION

• Position-wise shifts are +1, +2, +3, -4, -5.

• CAPUT: C+1=D, A+2=C, P+3=S, U-4=Q, T-5=O = DCSQO. ADOBO: A+1=B, D+2=F, O+3=R, B-4=X, O-5=J = BFRXJ.

• DESKS: D+1=E, E+2=G, S+3=V, K-4=G, S-5=N = EGVGN.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Memorise the shift vector +1,+2,+3,-4,-5 and apply letter by letter.

NOTE

• Wrap around the alphabet when a shift crosses A or Z.

question:
A series is given with one term wrong. Select that wrong term from the given alternatives.

CD100, EH214, GM328, IP442, KT556, MX670
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. GM328.

GIVEN

• CD100, EH214, GM328, IP442, KT556, MX670

SOLUTION

• First letters C,E,G,I,K,M → +2 each (fine). Numbers 100,214,328,442,556,670 → +114 each (fine).

• Second letters should be +4 each: D(4),H(8),L(12),P(16),T(20),X(24). The 3rd should be L, not M.

• So GM328 should be GL328 → GM328 is wrong.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Check each column separately; the second-letter column breaks the +4 rhythm at M (should be L).

NOTE

• In multi-part terms, one part often carries the error while the others stay regular.

question:
A series is given with one term wrong. Select that wrong term from the given alternatives.

MPL50, OMP320, QJT590, SGX860, UDB1130, UZG1400
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. UZG1400.

GIVEN

• MPL50, OMP320, QJT590, SGX860, UDB1130, UZG1400

SOLUTION

• First letters M,O,Q,S,U,? → +2 each; the 6th should be W (not U).

• Second letters P,M,J,G,D,? → -3 each; the 6th should be A (not Z).

• Third letters L,P,T,X,B,? → +4 each; the 6th should be F (not G). Numbers +270 (1400 fine).

• So the last term should be WAF1400 → UZG1400 is wrong.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Extend each column (+2, -3, +4) to the 6th term = W, A, F; only UZG1400 fails all three.

NOTE

• Treat every letter position and the number as independent arithmetic progressions.
